title: 2-Minute vs 2-Day Vegan Chocolate Chip Cookies
summary: In this Goodful video, Merle presents two vegan chocolate chip cookie approaches side by side: a fast 2-minute version baked in the microwave and a 2-day, flavor-deepened version that builds toffee, crushed chocolate, and an oats-brown-butter dough, chilled for 48 hours before baking. The quick method relies on refined coconut oil, light brown sugar, vanilla, and applesauce to form a dough that comes together with flour and chips before microwaving on a prepared plate. The 2-day method introduces a separate toffee element (vegan butter, brown sugar, salt, cooked to 290°F/143°C), oats hydrated with boiling water, browned Miyoko’s butter emulsified with ice and water, and a sugar-bath dough enriched with espresso powder, vanilla, and flour. The dough is folded with crushed toffee and chocolate, chilled for 48 hours, portioned into balls, baked at 325°F (160°C) for 18–20 minutes, and finished with a cohesive balance of sweetness, salt, toffee crunch, and chocolate. The video highlights ingredient choices, texture and flavor development, and timing strategies—showing that patience yields a noticeably richer vegan cookie.

sections.title: Two-minute vegan chocolate chip cookies
sections.description: Demonstrates a rapid 2-minute vegan cookie using refined coconut oil, light brown sugar, vanilla, and applesauce folded with flour and chocolate chips, formed into a mound on a buttered plate, and microwaved until set. Emphasizes the importance of using refined coconut oil to avoid coconut flavor and shows simple dough batching on a single plate for a fast result.

crushing toffee and chocolate into dough
sections.description: Outlines the multi-step 2-day cookie process. Starts with toffee preparation (butter, brown sugar, salt) on parchment, cooked to 290°F and then frozen. Builds dough by hydrating oats, browning Miyoko’s butter, emulsifying with ice, combining sugars with espresso powder, vanilla, and then folding in flour. After the dough comes together, the toffee is crushed and folded in with crushed chocolate. The dough is chilled for 48 hours to develop flavor and structure before scooping and baking.

sections.title: Bake and finish: two-day cookies
concepts: shaping dough into balls (1/3 cup scoop)
sections.description: Covers final steps: shaping chilled dough into balls, baking at 325°F (160°C) for 18–20 minutes, and tasting the finished cookies. Highlights the flavor balance of toffee, salt, and chocolate as a payoff for the 48-hour wait, and notes the cookies’ texture and aroma as a result of the extended, flavor-developing process.
